canonical.name: The top-order part of an order-m scalar operator depends only on the first derivative of a smooth coordinate change, while all higher derivatives of the coordinate map contribute only lower-order terms
Multiplying a defining function by a nonvanishing factor does not change whether a hypersurface is characteristic because the principal symbol is homogeneous
In the transport setting, differentiating the Volterra equation in the initial position gives a linearized system whose solution is the Jacobian of the characteristic flow
The stationary equation x dot Du = u reduces along each ray to an ordinary differential equation and therefore has radial characteristic solutions away from the origin
Homogeneous transport cannot create support away from the characteristic image of the initial support
A constant-coefficient hyperbolic principal part is diagonalized by choosing coordinates adapted to its two characteristic directions
The Tricomi operator and a fourth-order principal part show that the elliptic-parabolic-hyperbolic trichotomy is neither pointwise global nor applicable to arbitrary orders
Higher-order characteristic geometry is phrased in terms of covectors and hypersurfaces before any first-order transport flow produces characteristic curves
